variants.candidate: You build to keep rather than to show, and the things you go after slowly are usually the ones that stay yours.
variants.original: You build by tending ground, patient claims that compound, and your fortune favors what you can hold for years over what you can grab today.

variants.candidate: You hold yourself up by growing, so you feel strongest while something is being built and restless once it is finished.
variants.original: You recover by growing, and stillness drains you faster than effort ever will, so your health runs on having something alive to tend.

variants.candidate: You understand things by soaking in them rather than studying them, and your best decisions come after a night's sleep instead of a second search.
variants.original: Your thinking absorbs like rain into roots, slow and total, and what you learn deeply once feeds you for decades.

variants.candidate: You come alive when something you made gets seen, and most weeks you judge yourself by how much of you got out.
variants.original: What you have grown quietly wants a stage, and the warmth you release when you finally speak is what people remember you by.

variants.candidate: You grow best with a line to grow against, and you finish more under someone else's rule than under your own plan.
variants.original: Discipline reaches you as a blade, exacting people, hard standards, and every cut you accept on purpose becomes shape you get to keep.
